scenes.heading: Storage Layers
scenes.narration: Storage layers separate data by processing stage and access pattern, balancing cost, speed, and reliability.

scenes.heading: Layers by purpose
bullets: Landing or raw for immutable ingested data.
Archive and tiering for cold, rarely used data.
scenes.narration: The landing layer keeps raw data immutable for auditing and reprocessing. Staging holds intermediate results while transformations run. The curated layer serves clean data to consumers, and archival tiers move cold data to cheaper storage to control cost.

scenes.heading: Hot vs cold storage
scenes.narration: Hot storage keeps active data on fast media because low latency justifies the higher price. Cold storage parks rarely touched data on inexpensive tiers where slower retrieval is acceptable. Tiering data by access frequency can cut storage bills dramatically without losing anything.

scenes.heading: Lifecycle across layers
scenes.narration: Data enters through the raw landing layer and is preserved intact. It moves into staging for transformation, then to the curated layer once trustworthy. Over time, lifecycle policies age older data into cheaper archive tiers automatically.

scenes.text: Storage layers organize data by stage and access pattern, so you pay for speed only where it matters and keep raw data safe.
scenes.narration: Matching each layer to its access pattern is one of the simplest ways to control both cost and complexity at scale.
